hypotheses.justification: It is an argument because it is instance-implicit and mentions only `𝕜`, which is already an argument. The current proof uses it only indirectly, through mem_openSegment_translate → vadd_openSegment → image_openSegment → openSegment_eq_image, which uses order lemmas such as lt_add_of_pos_left and sub_pos. The statement itself is pure algebra. By definition, openSegment 𝕜 x y = {z | ∃ α β, 0 < α ∧ 0 < β ∧ α + β = 1 ∧ α • x + β • y = z}. When α + β = 1, smul_add, add_smul and one_smul give α • (a + b) + β • (a + c) = (α + β) • a + (α • b + β • c) = a + (α • b + β • c). Then add_left_cancel in the group E shows a + z ∈ openSegment 𝕜 (a+b) (a+c) ↔ z ∈ openSegment 𝕜 b c, with the same witnesses α, β in both directions, so the conditions 0 < α, 0 < β carry over unchanged. Nothing compares sums in 𝕜, so only Ring 𝕜, PartialOrder 𝕜, AddCommGroup E and Module 𝕜 E are needed. Degenerate cases (trivial 𝕜, or no elements strictly between 0 and 1) are covered: both sides are empty together. New proof under `omit [AddRightMono 𝕜] in`: Set.ext, unfold openSegment, rewrite with smul_add, ← add_smul, the hypothesis α + β = 1 and one_smul, and finish with add_right_inj.
